'''Shimazu no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''shimazu no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''shimazu kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled {{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国}}.

== Overview ==
=== Ancestry ===
*According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu|lt_ja=成務朝}}, '''{{ill|Izumo-Kasaya-no-Mikoto|ja|出雲笠夜命}}''', grandson of {{ill|Sahini-no-Sukune|ja|佐比邇足尼}} — of the same ancestral line as the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|出雲国造}} — was appointed Shimazu no Kuni no Miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
'''{{ill|Shima clan|ja|島氏}}''' (''shima-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} of {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}), of the same kin as the {{ill|Futakata no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|二方国造}}. Even after the end of the kuni-no-miyatsuko system they served as {{ill|district chiefs|ja|郡領}} of {{ill|Tōshi District|ja|答志郡}} into the {{ill|medieval period|ja|中世}}.<ref>{{ill|Ōta Akira|ja|太田亮}}, "Shima" in ''Seishi Kakei Daijiten'', 1936, p. 2846.</ref> Based on their genealogy and the "Kokuzō Hongi" entry, they are generally regarded as of the same kin as the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|出雲国造|lt=Izumo-no-Omi}}.

== Base ==
=== Territory ===
The kuni no miyatsuko's territory was the region then known as '''Shima(zu) Province''', later '''{{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国}}''' — present-day {{ill|Shima region|ja|志摩地方|lt=Shima region}} of {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県}}.

== Tutelary deity ==
'''{{ill|Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮}}''', the {{ill|ichinomiya|ja|一宮}} of {{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国}}, located in the former {{ill|Tōshi District|ja|答志郡}}.

=== Related shrines ===
* {{ill|Saminaga Shrine|ja|佐美長神社}} (''saminaga jinja'')
*:A {{ill|shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} located in Eriharachō, {{ill|Isobechō|ja|磯部町恵利原|lt=Isobechō Eriharachō}}, {{ill|Shima, Mie|ja|志摩市|lt=Shima City}}. Like the kin Futakata no Kuni no Miyatsuko, it enshrines {{ill|Ōtoshi-no-Kami|ja|大年神|lt=Ōtoshi-no-Kami|lt_ja=大歳神}}.<ref name="houga" />
